messages:
jaime_r: Hi all  need help. My custody agreement changed and starting 7/1 my ex will be the primary residential parent. Can I move our child off Redwood coverage to their stepparent's employer plan without waiting for open enrollment? What docs do you need?

annelise (People Ops): Sorry to hear about the churn, Jaime. You can change dependent coverage after a qualifying life event like change in custody. Well need a copy of the court order or signed custody agreement showing the effective date, plus the Dependent Change Form.

jaime_r: Do I have to terminate coverage on a specific date? Ex wants coverage to start 7/1, so ideally remove from our plan 6/30 and have them enroll 7/1.

jamal (Benefits): That timeline is fine. Steps we usually do: 1) Employee submits Dependent Change Form + custody order (scan). 2) We terminate dependent on your Redwood plan effective the day before the new coverage starts (6/30). 3) We provide a termination letter if the other employer carrier needs proof to accept enrollment.

payroll-bot: Payroll reminder: changes entered before Wednesday 11:59pm PT are applied to next payroll run. If termination is retroactive to a payroll already processed, refund/adjustment posts on subsequent cycle (can take 1-2 pay periods).

jaime_r: If I remove them, will they be eligible for COBRA? I don't want them stuck without coverage if ex's plan falls through.

jamal (Benefits): Good question. When a dependent loses eligibility due to a custody change/divorce, they may be eligible for COBRA continuation from Redwood's plan. COBRA is a separate election the dependent makes; carrier or COBRA vendor typically sends election notices. We can trigger the termination and notify the carrier so COBRA paperwork is generated. If the ex's employer needs proof of prior coverage to accept a special enrollment, we can provide a carrier letter.

maria (Legal): A couple of notes from legal: please redact any sensitive information not needed on copies shared in Slack. Use the secure email benefits@redwood.com for docs. Also if there's a court order with sealed details, send only the page that confirms custody transfer or have benefits advise on redaction.

jaime_r: Got it. Does Rippling let me pick the termination effective date? Or do you need to make the change?

annelise (People Ops): You can start the process in Rippling: Benefits -> Manage Dependents -> Remove dependent and choose effective date. But we still ask for the form + custody docs by email so Benefits retains legal records. If you prefer, we can file it for you once you attach docs.

jamal (Benefits): Also note carriers sometimes require proof of the new plan (insurance card or enrollment confirmation) if the dependent is moving to a different employer plan via a special enrollment. Ask the other employer for a letter or proof of pending coverage. That makes the handoff smoother and avoids COBRA overlap.

jaime_r: Other employer already asked for a termination letter to approve mid-year enrollment. Can you generate that?

annelise (People Ops): Yes we can provide a carrier termination letter once we submit the change. Typical turnaround 1-3 business days after we have your signed form + custody document. Include the name of the other plan and contact/email for the other employer/plan admin when you email.

payroll-bot: Action logged: custody-based dependent change request 1770102468. Please attach docs to benefits@redwood.com.

jaime_r: Thanks team. Uploading Dependent Change Form + custody order to benefits@redwood.com now and cc'ing the other plan contact. Appreciate the help.

jamal (Benefits): We'll confirm when the carrier sends the termination confirmation and share the termination letter for the other employer. If COBRA notice gets generated, we'll forward instructions.

jaime_r: Great. Will watch for confirmations. Appreciate the quick guidance.
